title: Registering with the RT — who does what to whom
goal: Report to your neighbourhood head and deal with office paperwork, and master the two ways Indonesian puts the object first: *Formulir ini harus Mbak isi* and *Surat itu dibuat oleh kelurahan*.
bekal: put the object first when the doer is *saya, kamu* or a "you" word: *Sudah Mbak bawa?*, *harus saya isi*
use the *di-* passive, with or without *oleh*, for everyone else: *dibuat oleh kelurahan*
understand and give polite passive instructions: *Tolong diisi*, *Mohon ditandatangani*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Lapor ke Pak RT
dialogs.intro: A few days after the painting. Every newcomer to an Indonesian neighbourhood should report to the head of the RT, the smallest unit of local administration. Sarah goes round to Pak Harjo's house after the sunset prayer, with a folder of photocopies.

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Silakan duduk, Mbak Sarah. Bu Endang sudah banyak cerita tentang Mbak.
lines.id: Please sit down. Bu Endang has told me a lot about you.
lines.literal: please sit, Miss Sarah. Mrs Endang already much tell about miss.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Terima kasih, Pak. Saya mau lapor sebagai warga baru.
lines.id: Thank you. I've come to register as a new resident.
lines.literal: thank you, sir. I want report as resident new.

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Bagus, Mbak. Setiap warga baru memang harus lapor ke RT.
lines.id: Good. Every new resident is supposed to report to the RT.
lines.literal: good, miss. every resident new indeed must report to RT.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Dokumen apa saja yang harus saya bawa?
lines.id: Which documents do I need to bring?
lines.literal: document what just which must I bring?

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Fotokopi paspor dan KITAS. Sudah Mbak bawa?
lines.id: Copies of your passport and KITAS. Have you brought them?
lines.literal: photocopy passport and KITAS. already miss bring?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Sudah, Pak. Ini fotokopinya. Surat kontrak rumah juga saya bawa.
lines.id: Yes. Here are the copies. I've brought the house contract too.
lines.literal: already, sir. this photocopy-the. letter contract house also I bring.

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Bagus. Formulir ini harus Mbak isi dulu, lalu Mbak tanda tangan di bawah.
lines.id: Good. You need to fill in this form first, then sign at the bottom.
lines.literal: good. form this must miss fill first, then miss sign at below.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Nomor HP saya juga ditulis di sini, Pak?
lines.id: Do I put my mobile number here too?
lines.literal: number HP my also be-written at here, sir?

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Nggih, supaya Mbak bisa dihubungi oleh pengurus RT kalau ada apa-apa.
lines.id: Yes, so the RT committee can contact you if anything happens.
lines.literal: yes, so-that miss can be-contacted by committee RT if exist what-what.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Baik. Lalu data saya dibawa ke mana, Pak?
lines.id: Right. And where do my details go after that?
lines.literal: good. then data my be-brought to where, sir?

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Data Mbak nanti saya bawa ke kelurahan. Surat keterangan domisilinya dibuat oleh kelurahan, kira-kira seminggu.
lines.id: I'll take your details to the kelurahan. They make the certificate of residence; it takes about a week.
lines.literal: data miss later I bring to kelurahan. letter statement domicile-the be-made by kelurahan, roughly one-week.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Oh, bagus. Surat itu memang diminta oleh kantor saya.
lines.id: Oh, good. My office has actually asked for that letter.
lines.literal: oh, good. letter that indeed be-asked by office my.

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Satu lagi, Mbak. Iuran kebersihan dan keamanan dibayar setiap bulan, tiga puluh ribu.
lines.id: One more thing. The rubbish and security fee is paid monthly: thirty thousand.
lines.literal: one more, miss. contribution cleanliness and security be-paid every month, three ten thousand.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Siap, Pak. Iurannya saya bayar ke siapa?
lines.id: Of course. Who do I pay it to?
lines.literal: ready, sir. contribution-the I pay to who?

lines.speaker: Harjo:
lines.text: Ke Bu Endang saja. Beliau bendahara RT kita.
lines.id: Just give it to Bu Endang. She's our RT treasurer.
lines.literal: to Mrs Endang just. she treasurer RT our.

notes: **RT** (said *ér-té*) is *Rukun Tetangga*, the neighbourhood association: a few dozen households with an elected, unpaid head, the *ketua RT*, usually just called *Pak RT*. Several RTs make an *RW*. The RT is the first stop for almost anything official, from a residence letter to a wedding.

**Lapor** means to report. Newcomers, and traditionally even overnight guests, are reported to the RT. In a Yogya kampung it is also a social introduction: by the end of the visit Pak Harjo knows where Sarah works, and by tomorrow so will everyone else.

**KITAS** is *Kartu Izin Tinggal Terbatas*, the limited stay permit card that working foreigners hold; Unit 14 takes Sarah to extend it. Always carry photocopies: every office wants one, and originals handed over tend to come back slowly.

**Tanda tangan** is a signature, literally "hand sign", and *tanda tangan di sini* is "sign here". The formal verb is *menandatangani* (to sign something), with the passive *ditandatangani*: *Formulir ini harus ditandatangani.*

**Kelurahan** is the urban village office, one level above the RW; its head is the *lurah*. In the countryside the equivalent is the *desa*, run by a *kepala desa*. **Surat keterangan domisili**, a certificate of residence, is what employers and banks ask foreigners for.

**Beliau bendahara RT kita.** *Beliau* is the respectful "he, she" for elders and people of standing. *Iuran* is a regular contribution; in a kampung it pays for rubbish collection and the night watch (*ronda*), which the men of the RT take turns to keep.

grammars.title: Object first: Formulir ini harus Mbak isi
body: When the doer is *saya*, *kamu*, *kita* or a word used for "you" (*Mbak, Mas, Bapak, Ibu*), Indonesian likes to put the object first, then the doer, then the bare root. No *me-*, no *di-*.

head: Active
Object first
English
rows: You must fill in this form.
Who do I pay it to?

after: ⚠️ Words like *sudah, belum, harus, akan, bisa* go **before** the doer: *harus Mbak isi*, *sudah saya bawa*. Nothing may come between the doer and the verb. (*Mbak harus isi formulir ini* also exists, but that is just a casual active sentence with the *me-* dropped.)
This is not a rare literary form. In offices it is the most normal way to talk about paperwork, and it sounds more natural than an active sentence stuffed with *me-* verbs.

grammars.title: The di- passive, with or without oleh
body: For any other doer, whether a person, *dia*, *beliau* or an institution, put *di-* on the root and, if you want to name the doer, add *oleh* ("by").

head: Active
Passive
English
rows: The letter is made by the kelurahan.
My office has asked for it.
Pak Harjo wrote that number down.

after: *Oleh* can be dropped when the doer comes straight after the verb, as in the last row. When the doer doesn't matter, leave it out altogether, as in the fourth.
⚠️ With *saya* and *kamu*, avoid *di- … oleh*: *Surat itu ditulis oleh saya* is understood but sounds clumsy, and any editor will change it to *Surat itu saya tulis*.

dialogs.title: Second dialogue — Berkas karyawan
dialogs.intro: Next morning at the office. Mbak Nur, the office manager, is putting together Sarah's personnel file, and nothing gets past her.

lines.speaker: Nur:
lines.text: Mbak Sarah, berkas untuk HRD sudah lengkap?
lines.id: Mbak Sarah, is your file for HR complete?
lines.literal: Miss Sarah, file for HRD already complete?

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Sudah, Mbak. Fotokopi paspor dan KITAS sudah saya kumpulkan kemarin.
lines.id: Yes. I handed in the passport and KITAS copies yesterday.
lines.literal: already, miss. photocopy passport and KITAS already I hand-in yesterday.

lines.speaker: Nur:
lines.text: Betul, sudah saya terima. Tapi surat domisili belum Mbak serahkan.
lines.id: Yes, I've got those. But you haven't handed in the residence letter.
lines.literal: correct, already I receive. but letter domicile not-yet miss hand-over.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Surat itu sedang dibuat oleh kelurahan. Kata Pak Harjo, seminggu lagi.
lines.id: The kelurahan is making it now. Pak Harjo says it'll be another week.
lines.literal: letter that in-process be-made by kelurahan. word Mr Harjo, one-week more.

lines.speaker: Nur:
lines.text: Baik. Kalau sudah jadi, tolong langsung diserahkan ke saya, ya.
lines.id: Fine. When it's ready, please give it straight to me.
lines.literal: good. if already ready, please directly be-handed to me, yes.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Siap, Mbak. Ada lagi yang harus saya isi?
lines.id: Will do. Is there anything else I need to fill in?
lines.literal: ready, miss. exist more which must I fill?

lines.speaker: Nur:
lines.text: Formulir data karyawan ini. Halaman dua belum diisi, dan belum ditandatangani.
lines.id: This staff details form. Page two hasn't been filled in, and it hasn't been signed.
lines.literal: form data employee this. page two not-yet be-filled, and not-yet be-signed.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Aduh, maaf. Halaman dua saya lewati. Sekarang saya isi, ya.
lines.id: Oh no, sorry. I skipped page two. I'll fill it in now.
lines.literal: ouch, sorry. page two I skip. now I fill, yes.

lines.speaker: Nur:
lines.text: Silakan. Setelah itu, formulirnya dikirim ke kantor Jakarta oleh bagian HRD.
lines.id: Go ahead. After that, HR will send the form to the Jakarta office.
lines.literal: please. after that, form-the be-sent to office Jakarta by section HRD.

lines.speaker: Sarah:
lines.text: Nanti dibaca oleh Pak Hendra juga?
lines.id: Will Pak Hendra read it too?
lines.literal: later be-read by Mr Hendra also?

lines.speaker: Nur:
lines.text: Pasti. Semua berkas karyawan baru diperiksa sendiri oleh beliau.
lines.id: Certainly. He checks every new employee's file himself.
lines.literal: surely. all file employee new be-examined self by him.

notes: **HRD** (said *ha-ér-dé*) is the human resources department, from English "human resources development"; the older Indonesian term is *bagian personalia*. Indonesian offices are full of English abbreviations pronounced with Indonesian letter names.

**Sudah saya terima** — Mbak Nur speaks in object-first sentences almost without thinking: *sudah saya terima*, *belum Mbak serahkan*. This is what careful office Indonesian sounds like, and why the pattern is worth making automatic.
**Kalau sudah jadi** — *jadi* once more, now meaning "ready, finished" of something being made: *Suratnya sudah jadi?* (is the letter ready?), *Bajunya belum jadi* (the dress isn't finished yet).

**Tolong langsung diserahkan ke saya** — a request in the passive. Indonesians often ask for things by describing what should happen to the object rather than ordering the person to act. It is softer than *Tolong serahkan*, and very common from managers.

**Aduh** is the all-purpose "ouch, oh no": for pain, for mistakes, for bad news. *Saya lewati* is "I skipped it" (*lewat* = to pass; *melewati* = to pass something). Notice that Sarah owns up in an object-first sentence too.

**Diperiksa sendiri oleh beliau** — *sendiri* after a verb means "personally, himself". Mbak Nur uses *beliau* for Pak Hendra though he is in Jakarta: respect for a senior person doesn't depend on whether he can hear you.

grammars.title: Tolong di-: polite instructions in the passive
body: Forms, notices and polite managers all prefer the passive for instructions. Learn to read these at a glance, and use the spoken ones yourself.
after: *Mohon* and *harap* are the formal cousins of *tolong*, and Unit 15 is devoted to them. For now, notice how the English command ("sign") becomes an Indonesian description ("be signed"): the instruction is aimed at the paper, not at you.

blocks.text: Indonesian administration is a ladder, and newcomers start on the bottom rung. The two lowest rungs are run by unpaid neighbours; above them are civil servants.

head: Level
Headed by
You go there for
rows: reporting in, cover letters, local news
a second signature on RT letters

blocks.text: Yogyakarta has a twist: it is a *Daerah Istimewa* (Special Region), and its governor is the Sultan of Yogyakarta rather than an elected politician. People are proud of it, and *Jogja Istimewa* (Jogja is special) is printed on T-shirts all over town.
